summary: Elevated P95 latency and 504s on dedicated pool — node-level interference + autoscale gap
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:22 UTC, Ledgerly reported intermittent p95 latency spikes and an increase in 504/timeout responses for requests routed to their dedicated GPU pool in eu-west-1. Surface metrics show sustained p50 ~150ms but p95 jumping from ~220ms baseline to 1.2-1.6s during spikes, and a burst of 504s coincident with those spikes. Impact: customer-facing feature degraded; higher error rate and user-visible latency. Hypothesis: localized GPU contention (noisy neighbor) on one or two nodes combined with autoscaler not reacting quickly enough (min_replicas/config mismatch), leading to request queueing and timeouts.
impact: Customer Ledgerly (dedicated) experienced increased end-user errors (504) and latency regressions in production across their dedicated pool. Estimated affected traffic: ~18% of requests to the pool during incident windows. Business impact: reduced throughput on key feature and customer escalated to CS.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Route load similar to Ledgerly synthetic workload to their dedicated pool (burst QPS pattern: 350 req/s sustained with 700 req/s spikes for 60s).
2) Observe p50/p95 and error rates in Redwood Console per-route dashboard.
3) Correlate node-level GPU utilization and process-level metrics for serving-runtime.
4) If autoscaler min_replicas is set below observed steady-state required replicas for burst, queue depth increases and timeouts occur.
observed_metrics_and_logs:
- From 2026-03-10T08:22 to 08:40 UTC: p95 jump to 1.2-1.6s, 504 rate increased from 0.01% to 3.8%.
- Node metrics: node-12 GPU0 util spiked to 96% with GPU memory at 98% on card-3; node-19 showed erratic mem peaks.
- Serving runtime logs: repeated KV cache misses + repeated context switching logs for worker threads.
- Scheduler logs: observed pending queue length increase on pool ledgerly-dedicated-1.
- Autoscaler events: no scale-up triggered during initial 120s of burst; scale decision log shows threshold evaluation did not exceed configured burst_threshold due to short window and conservative cooldown (300s).
investigation_notes:
- Hypothesis A (noisy neighbor): GPU card saturation on node-12 caused local slowdown for other tenants pinned to same card set. Evidence: disproportionate latency from requests routed via node-12; SRE repro'ed latency by isolating node-12.
- Hypothesis B (autoscale misconfiguration): min_replicas set to 2 for this pool while observed baseline needs 4-5 replicas for burst headroom; autoscaler cooldown and evaluation window prevented fast ramp to required capacity.
- Telemetry: sampling of tracing indicates increased dispatch queuing time rather than model execution time for many slow requests, suggesting queueing at runtime ingress.
- No evidence of model-level regression (same model versions and weights served elsewhere without elevated latencies).
- Spot checks of NVIDIA driver logs show no ECC errors or kernel OOM, but cgroup throttling logs present on node-12.
- Cross-tenant attribution: tenant id mapping shows two new bigger tenants placed on same physical rack 24 hours prior — possible scheduling regression in allocator.
timeline:
2026-03-10 08:15 UTC - Ledgerly first reported elevated p95 and sporadic 504s.
2026-03-10 08:22 UTC - Alerts triggered for p95>1s and error-rate>1% on ledgerly pool.
2026-03-10 08:30 UTC - CS created ticket SUP-73621 and escalated to SRE.
2026-03-10 08:45 UTC - SRE identified node-12 as hot spot; temporarily cordoned node-12 from serving rotation.
2026-03-10 09:02 UTC - Metrics improved after cordon; p95 returned near baseline and 504s subsided.
2026-03-10 11:10 UTC - Autoscaler policy reviewed; found conservative cooldown and low min_replicas.
2026-03-11 10:00 UTC - Deploy short-term mitigation: increase min_replicas to 4 for ledgerly pool and reduce cooldown to 60s for bursty_workloads label.
2026-03-12 14:00 UTC - Longer-term followups scheduled: change scheduler packing policy to avoid aggressive co-location for large tenants and add noisy-neighbor detection alerting.
root_cause: Primary root cause: combination of a noisy-tenant causing high GPU utilization on specific nodes (node-12) and an autoscaler configuration that had too-low min_replicas and a long cooldown. The scheduler placed multiple heavy tenants on the same rack which amplified the contention. Queueing at the runtime ingress and cgroup throttling contributed to increased p95 and request timeouts.
resolution_and_workaround:
Short-term: cordoned hot node (node-12) to drain serving traffic; increased min_replicas to 4 for ledgerly-dedicated pool; reduced autoscaler cooldown to 60s for pools labeled bursty_workloads. Result: p95 and 504 rates returned to baseline for observed windows.
Medium-term: adjust scheduler bin-packing heuristics to limit co-located large tenants on same physical cards; add autoscaler policy template for dedicated pools serving bursty workloads.
Long-term: implement noisy-neighbor detector that triggers automatic migration or temporary isolation and add capacity-based pre-scaling during known customer traffic windows.
postmortem_actions:
- Create scheduler change PR to add tenant-size-aware placement (PR linked).
- Add an observability alert for per-card cgroup throttling and sudden per-node memory pressure.
- Update Dedicated best-practices doc for customers: recommend min_replicas based on historical p95 and burst patterns.
- Follow-up ticket INT-4452 opened to track scheduler allocator changes.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:38 UTC - Marcus Ortiz (SRE): Identified node-12 as primary offender; cordoning now. Initial cordon shows immediate p95 improvement. Will keep monitoring.

2026-03-10 09:10 UTC - Ava Chen (CS): Informed Ledgerly that we're investigating and performed a temporary mitigation (cordon). Customer reports partial relief; they requested timeline for permanent fix.

2026-03-10 11:20 UTC - SRE Lead (Priya Nair): Autoscaler cooldown of 300s is too conservative for bursty traffic. Proposal: reduce to 60s for pools with label bursty_workloads; need config change and rollout. Linking config PR.
2026-03-11 09:50 UTC - Marcus Ortiz: Increased min_replicas to 4 and reduced cooldown to 60s in staging; running soak tests. No regressions observed so far.
2026-03-12 16:05 UTC - Ledgerly (customer comment): Thank you for the quick workaround. We'll monitor and provide feedback. Please keep us updated on scheduler placement changes.
